question: After companion-side denylist revocation is complete, should OpenClaw permanently support denylist policy in both tools.exec configuration and exec-approvals.json, overriding full/off and durable trust?
rationale: The remaining code defect has a bounded repair, but the lasting persisted policy, protocol, fail-closed, and operator-impact semantics require maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt both layers
options.body: Keep both policy sources with final companion revalidation and one-shot approvals.

options.title: Approvals file only
options.body: Remove tools.exec.denylist and keep the STOP list under the existing approvals store.

options.title: Decline denylist policy
options.body: Retain the existing deny, allowlist, and full modes without deny-by-exception behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt both layers
recommendation.body: Keep both policy sources with final companion revalidation and one-shot approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history makes this person the strongest available owner for companion authorization, revocation, and permanent security-policy semantics.
